info.title: Zendiloos API
info.description: Management API of the Zendiloos NAS operating system.

get.summary: All accounts, ordered by name.

post.summary: Creates an account with its Linux user and SMB password.

delete.summary: Deletes another account with its Linux user. Its files stay.

patch.summary:
Changes another account's full name, role or whether it is enabled.
Disabling ends its sessions and SMB access, and keeps it out of the
shares' files as if denied (NFS): the files of the shares it could use
follow in the background.

post.summary:
Sets a new password for another account, which must change it at its
next login. Ends its sessions.

delete.summary:
Turns another account's second factor off, for someone who lost their
phone and their recovery codes. Ends that account's sessions.

204.description: Off: the password alone signs in.

get.summary: Every app of every catalog, by name. Needs `containers.manage`.

One app of a catalog, with what it needs from the NAS. Needs
`containers.manage`.

post.summary:
Fills in an app's Compose file, its template, with the values given and
the caller as the account its containers run as; the devices the machine
lacks are left out. Nothing is made yet. Needs `containers.manage`.

get.summary:
The app's icon, a PNG checked when it was fetched. Needs
`containers.manage`.

Whether apps can run: Docker installed, its data on a pool. Needs
`containers.manage`.

post.summary:
Puts Docker's data (images, containers) on a pool; Docker restarts.
Needs `containers.manage`.

409.description: `refused`: Docker missing, or its data on another pool

post.summary:
Installs Docker from Debian (`docker.io`, `docker-compose`) and puts
its data on a pool, as a job; apps can be installed afterwards. Needs
`containers.manage`.

get.summary:
The apps installed the earlier way, with what Docker makes of them.
Needs `containers.manage`.
One installed app. Needs `containers.manage`.

delete.summary:
Removes an app with its containers, images and data, then its access
to shares and its account, as a job. Needs `containers.manage`.

get.summary: The last lines its containers wrote. Needs `containers.manage`.

parameters.name: lines
parameters.description: The last this many lines, 1 to 5000; 200 if left out.

post.summary: Starts an installed app's containers. Needs `containers.manage`.
Stops an installed app's containers. Needs `containers.manage`.

get.summary:
The Docker projects made from apps of a catalog, by name, with where
they answer. Needs `containers.manage`.

The catalogs apps come from: the community catalog first. Needs
`containers.manage`.

post.summary:
Adds a catalog. It must answer with an index this version reads; its
apps are not reviewed by the community catalog. Needs
`containers.manage`.
Fetches every catalog again. Needs `containers.manage`.

delete.summary:
Removes a catalog; the community catalog stays. Needs
`containers.manage`.

post.summary:
Signs in with name and password. An account with a second factor gets
no session yet: the code follows at `/auth/login/second-factor`.

200.description: Signed in; the session cookie is set.

202.description: The password checked out; a code from the authenticator app is asked for.

401.description: `invalid_credentials`: also for a disabled account, which does not tell that the password was right

post.summary:
The second step of a sign-in: the code from the authenticator app, or a
recovery code. From the address the password came from, within five
minutes; three wrong codes end the sign-in.

200.description: Signed in; the session cookie is set.

401.description: `sign_in_expired`: sign in with the password again

post.summary: Ends the current session.

204.description: Signed out; the session cookie is removed.

post.summary: Changes the caller's password and ends their other sessions.

get.summary: The signed-in account and the CSRF token of this session.
Whether the signed-in account's sign-ins ask for a second factor.

post.summary:
Turns the second factor on with the first code from the app, from the
session that began the setup. Three wrong codes end the setup (the third
answers `no_two_factor_setup`). Ends the account's other sessions.

409.description: `no_two_factor_setup`: none waits for this session (none begun, begun elsewhere, over ten minutes ago or before a restart, ended by three wrong codes or a new password); `two_factor_on`

post.summary: Turns the signed-in account's second factor off. Ends its other sessions.

204.description: Off: the password alone signs in.

post.summary:
New recovery codes for the password and a code from the app; the old
ones stop working. Ends the account's other sessions.

Begins setting up the signed-in account's authenticator app, with its
password: a new secret, which waits ten minutes for its first code from
this session. One begun before is replaced. A wrong password counts as a
failed login. Not for an account whose password an administrator sets.

get.summary: The certificates. Needs `system.manage`.

post.summary:
Adds a certificate; it is issued with `POST /certificates/{id}/issue`.
Needs `system.manage`.

get.summary: The accounts at ACME servers. Needs `system.manage`.

post.summary:
Adds an account; it is registered with the server at its first
certificate. Needs `system.manage`.

put.summary: Changes an account. Needs `system.manage`.

delete.summary: Removes an account no certificate uses. Needs `system.manage`.

get.summary: The challenges certificates can use. Needs `system.manage`.

post.summary: Adds a challenge. Needs `system.manage`.

put.summary:
Changes a challenge; secrets left empty stay as they were. Needs
`system.manage`.

delete.summary: Removes a challenge no certificate uses. Needs `system.manage`.

get.summary:
Whether acme.sh is installed, and the DNS providers to choose from.
Needs `system.view`.

post.summary: Installs acme.sh from Debian, as a job. Needs `system.manage`.

put.summary:
Changes a certificate; it takes effect at its next issuance. Needs
`system.manage`.

delete.summary:
Removes a certificate the web interface does not show. Needs
`system.manage`.

post.summary:
Issues the certificate now (or again), as a job whose output is what
acme.sh writes. Needs `system.manage`.

409.description: `acme_not_installed`, or `refused`: an HTTP challenge without plain HTTP on port 80

post.summary:
Replaces a volume's contents with a backup, in a job: the archive is
checked against its record first. Needs `containers.manage`.

409.description: `volume_in_use`: running containers use it (named); `volume_busy`; `refused`: a backup that failed, or a volume not backed up here

post.summary:
Reads a Compose file as Compose would and names what it lets
containers do beyond themselves. Needs `containers.manage`.

409.description: `refused`: Compose cannot read it, in its words

get.summary: Every container, by name, with its newest use. Needs `containers.manage`.

One container as Docker inspects it now: its command, environment,
networks, mounts, privileges, limits and health check. Needs
`containers.manage`.

delete.summary: Removes a container that does not run. Needs `containers.manage`.

get.summary: The last lines a container wrote. Needs `containers.manage`.

parameters.name: lines
parameters.description: At most 10 000; 500 if absent.

get.summary:
The processes of a running container, `docker top`. Needs
`containers.manage`.

How updating a container would go: by its project, or only its image
fetched. Needs `containers.manage`.

409.description: `app_project`: an app installed the earlier way
`app_project`: an app installed the earlier way

post.summary: Starts, stops or restarts a container. Needs `containers.manage`.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: `start`, `stop` or `restart`

get.summary:
Where Docker's data is, and the pools it could go to. Needs
`containers.manage`.

post.summary:
Moves Docker's data to another pool, in a job: every container stops
meanwhile. Needs `containers.manage`.

409.description: `refused`: too little space, or not on a pool zendiloOS made

get.summary: Every image, the newest first. Needs `containers.manage`.

post.summary:
Removes every image no container uses; says what was freed. Needs
`containers.manage`.
Fetches an image, in a job. Needs `containers.manage`.

delete.summary: Removes an image no container uses. Needs `containers.manage`.

get.summary: Every network, Docker's own first. Needs `containers.manage`.

post.summary: Creates a bridge network. Needs `containers.manage`.

delete.summary: Removes a network no container is in. Needs `containers.manage`.

get.summary: The engine at a glance. Needs `containers.manage`.

The shares the caller may put a project's folder in. Needs
`containers.manage`.
Every Compose project, by name. Needs `containers.manage`.

post.summary:
Makes a project: writes its Compose file into the folder, with the
caller's permissions, and deploys it if asked. Needs `containers.manage`.

409.description: `project_exists`; `refused`: Compose cannot read it; `compose_risks`: not accepted

get.summary: One project. Needs `containers.manage`.

delete.summary:
Removes a project's containers and networks, in a job; images, data and
its folder stay. Not for an app of a catalog. Needs `containers.manage`.

get.summary:
A project's Compose files. Not for an app of a catalog: they hold its
generated settings. Needs `containers.manage`.

put.summary:
Writes a project's changed Compose file and deploys it again, in a job.
Only for a project made here. Needs `containers.manage`.

get.summary: The last lines of the project's containers. Needs `containers.manage`.

parameters.name: lines
parameters.description: At most 10 000; 500 if absent.

post.summary:
Brings the project up again in a job, recreating what changed and
removing containers no longer in its file; with `pull` (no body: no
pull), its images are fetched anew first. The job's `output` follows
what Docker Compose writes. Not for an app of a catalog. Needs
`containers.manage`.

409.description: `app_project`; `project_unconfirmed`: made before what was confirmed was kept, save its file once

post.summary:
Starts, stops or restarts a project's containers. Needs
`containers.manage`.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: `start`, `stop` or `restart`

get.summary:
The newest look for newer images, `null` before the first. Needs
`containers.manage`.

post.summary:
Updates every project with a newer image, in a job; `job` is `null` if
there is none. Apps of catalogs are the App Center's. Needs
`containers.manage`.
Asks the registries now. Needs `containers.manage`.

get.summary: When newer images are looked for and taken. Needs `containers.manage`.

put.summary: Sets them. Needs `containers.manage`.

get.summary:
What the containers used, sample by sample, oldest first. Needs
`containers.manage`.

parameters.name: seconds
parameters.description: How far back, at most twelve hours; one hour if absent.

parameters.name: containers
parameters.description: Container names, comma separated; all if absent.

get.summary:
Every volume, by name, with who uses it and how it is backed up. Needs
`containers.manage`.

post.summary:
Removes every volume no container uses, named ones too, with their
data; says what was freed. Needs `containers.manage`.

get.summary:
What each local volume's data takes up, counted on the NAS; takes a
while, so it is asked apart from the list. Needs `containers.manage`.

delete.summary:
Removes a volume no container uses, with its data and its backup plan;
its backups stay. Needs `containers.manage`.

409.description: `refused`: a container uses it; `volume_busy`: being backed up or restored

get.summary: The volume's backup plan. Needs `containers.manage`.

put.summary:
Makes or replaces the volume's backup plan: into a folder of a share
the administrator may write. Needs `containers.manage`.

403.description: `forbidden`, `csrf_rejected`; `share_denied`: a share the administrator may not write

409.description: `refused`: not a local volume with its data in Docker's folder

delete.summary:
Ends the volume's backup plan; its backups stay. Needs
`containers.manage`.

get.summary:
The volume's backups, the newest first: those kept, and the runs that
failed lately. Needs `containers.manage`.

post.summary:
Backs the volume up now as its plan says, in a job. Needs
`containers.manage`.

409.description: `volume_busy`: a backup or restore of it is under way

get.summary: Which file services run. Needs `system.view`.

put.summary:
Turns SMB and NFS on or off and sets the workgroup and the oldest SMB
version; applied with the shares at once. Needs `system.manage`.

409.description: `refused`: the host did not accept it; the previous settings apply

get.summary:
The signed-in account's favourite folders, in shares it may use.
Needs `files.read`.

put.summary: Replaces the signed-in account's favourite folders. Needs `files.read`.

404.description: `not_found`: a share the account may not use

get.summary:
Downloads a folder of a removable drive as a tar archive. Needs
`files.read` and `storage.manage`.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Relative to the share's root, e.g. `photos/2024`; empty for the root.

parameters.name: snapshot
parameters.description: In this snapshot of the share, read only (its label).

422.description: `invalid_operation`: not a folder, too many files

post.summary:
Deletes entries of a removable drive for good (a drive has no recycle
bin), as a job. Needs `files.write` and `storage.manage`.

get.summary:
Downloads a file from a removable drive, as from a share. Needs
`files.read` and `storage.manage`.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Relative to the share's root, e.g. `photos/2024/beach.jpg`.

parameters.name: inline
parameters.description:
Let the browser show the file, if it is a picture, sound, video or
plain text; anything else is saved regardless.

parameters.name: snapshot
parameters.description: From this snapshot of the share (its label).

416.description: The range starts beyond the end.

get.summary:
What a file or folder on a removable drive is, and for a folder what is
in it, counted as in a share. Needs `files.read` and `storage.manage`.

parameters.name: drive
parameters.description: The drive's ID, as `/storage/removable` lists it

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Relative to the share's root, e.g. `photos/2024`; empty for the root.

parameters.name: snapshot
parameters.description: In this snapshot of the share, read only (its label).

404.description: `not_found`: no such drive mounted, or nothing at that path

get.summary:
A folder's contents on a removable drive. Needs `files.read` and
`storage.manage`.

parameters.name: drive
parameters.description: The drive's ID, as `/storage/removable` lists it

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Relative to the share's root, e.g. `photos/2024`; empty for the root.

parameters.name: snapshot
parameters.description: In this snapshot of the share, read only (its label).

404.description: `not_found`: no such drive mounted, or no such folder

post.summary:
Creates a folder on a removable drive. Needs `files.write` and
`storage.manage`.

Renames a file or folder on a removable drive. Needs `files.write` and
`storage.manage`.

get.summary:
Looks for names in a folder of a removable drive and everything below
it, as in a share. Needs `files.read` and `storage.manage`.

parameters.name: drive
parameters.description: The drive's ID, as `/storage/removable` lists it

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The folder to search, with everything below it; empty for the root.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description:
What names contain, whatever the case: 1 to 255 bytes, no control
characters.

parameters.name: hidden
parameters.description: Also names starting with `.`, and what is in such folders.

parameters.name: snapshot
parameters.description: In this snapshot of the share, read only (its label).

404.description: `not_found`: no such drive mounted, or no such folder

422.description: `invalid_operation`: no text to look for, or too much

post.summary:
Copies or moves entries of a removable drive into a folder of it, of
another drive or of a share, as a job. What lands in a share is the
administrator's and takes the folder's permissions, as an upload does.
Needs `files.write` and `storage.manage`.

Uploads a file onto a removable drive. Needs `files.write` and
`storage.manage`.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The folder, relative to the share's root; empty for the root.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The new file's name.

parameters.name: replace
parameters.description: Replace a file of that name.

get.summary:
The signed-in user's personal folder, if they have one, then the
shares whose rules let them in. Needs `files.read`.

Downloads a folder with everything in it as a tar archive, which
Windows, macOS and Linux open without extra software. Refused if
anything inside cannot be read; the share's recycle bins are left out.
Its length is known ahead, so one that breaks off shows as a failed
download. Needs `files.read`.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Relative to the share's root, e.g. `photos/2024`; empty for the root.

parameters.name: snapshot
parameters.description: In this snapshot of the share, read only (its label).

422.description: `invalid_operation`: not a folder, too many files

post.summary:
Moves entries into the user's recycle bin if the share has one, deletes
them for good otherwise (and inside the recycle bin), as a job. Needs
`files.write`.

get.summary:
Downloads a file, as an attachment unless a harmless kind is asked for
`inline`. One byte range (`Range`) can be asked for, to resume a
download (`If-Range` with the `Last-Modified` given) or seek in a video.
Needs `files.read`.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Relative to the share's root, e.g. `photos/2024/beach.jpg`.

parameters.name: inline
parameters.description:
Let the browser show the file, if it is a picture, sound, video or
plain text; anything else is saved regardless.

parameters.name: snapshot
parameters.description: From this snapshot of the share (its label).

416.description: The range starts beyond the end.

get.summary:
What a file or folder is: when it was made and changed, whose it is;
for a folder, its files, folders and hidden entries counted below it
as the user may see them, and what the files hold. Walks as a search
does; at most ten million entries within half a minute, counted so far
when that is up or the request is dropped. Needs `files.read`.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Relative to the share's root, e.g. `photos/2024`; empty for the root.

parameters.name: snapshot
parameters.description: In this snapshot of the share, read only (its label).

404.description: `not_found`: no such share, or not shared with the user, or nothing at that path

get.summary: A folder's contents. Needs `files.read`.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Relative to the share's root, e.g. `photos/2024`; empty for the root.

parameters.name: snapshot
parameters.description: In this snapshot of the share, read only (its label).

404.description: `not_found`: no such share, or not shared with the user, or no such folder

post.summary: Creates a folder. Needs `files.write`.
Renames a file or folder. Needs `files.write`.

Moves entries out of the user's recycle bin back to where they were
deleted from; folders on the way are made again, and a taken name gets
a free one beside it. Stops at the first that fails. Needs `files.write`.

get.summary:
Looks for names in a folder and everything below it, as the user may
see them: not into links, other file systems, other people's recycle
bins (nor into the bins at all unless searched from inside one), and
never by a name that is not UTF-8. At most 500 entries within a few
seconds. Needs `files.read`.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The folder to search, with everything below it; empty for the root.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description:
What names contain, whatever the case: 1 to 255 bytes, no control
characters.

parameters.name: hidden
parameters.description: Also names starting with `.`, and what is in such folders.

parameters.name: snapshot
parameters.description: In this snapshot of the share, read only (its label).

404.description: `not_found`: no such share, or not shared with the user, or no such folder

422.description: `invalid_operation`: no text to look for, or too much

get.summary:
The share's snapshots, newest first: what it looked like then. Needs
`files.read`.

post.summary:
Copies entries out of a snapshot back into the share, each into the
folder it was in; a name that is taken gets `name (2).ext`, so nothing
is replaced. As a job. Needs `files.write`.

Copies or moves entries into a folder, possibly of another share, as a
job. A copy whose name is taken gets a free one, `name (2).ext`; a move
fails. Needs `files.write`.

Uploads a file: the request body, unchanged, any size the volume has
room for. Written under a hidden name and renamed when complete. Needs
`files.write`.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The folder, relative to the share's root; empty for the root.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The new file's name.

parameters.name: replace
parameters.description: Replace a file of that name.

get.summary:
The volumes with their folders, for the file manager's tree. Someone
who manages shares (`shares.manage`) sees every volume and every folder
on it, those they may not open marked; everyone else only the folders
they may use, and the volumes holding one. Needs `files.read`.
All groups, ordered by name.

post.summary: Creates a group with its Linux group.

delete.summary: Deletes a group with its Linux group.

patch.summary:
Changes a group's description or members. The change stands at once;
the files of the shares it touches follow in the background.

get.summary: Liveness check for monitoring and the reverse proxy.
get.description:
Public, so it deliberately reveals nothing about the system, not even the
software version.

get.summary: Where the personal folders are and who has one. Needs `users.manage`.

put.summary: Turns personal folders on, on a pool, or off. Needs `users.manage`.

409.description: `refused`: e.g. a share is called home

put.summary:
Gives an account a personal folder, changes its quota or takes it away
(its files stay). Needs `users.manage`.

get.summary:
The most recent jobs, newest first. Changes arrive on the WebSocket
topic `jobs`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most 200; 50 if absent.

get.summary: One job.
A page of the audit log: who did what, newest first.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most 500; 200 if absent.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: `older` of the previous page.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Only entries of this action, such as `identity.login`.

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.description: Only entries whose action starts so, such as `containers.`.

get.summary: A page of the system journal, newest first.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Which view; `system` if absent.

parameters.name: priority
parameters.description: This priority and everything more severe; `info` if absent.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most 500; 200 if absent.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: `older` of the previous page, for the entries before it.

get.summary:
Interfaces, addresses, default routes and name servers. Needs
`system.view`.

post.summary: Keeps the change that waits for confirmation. Needs `system.manage`.

put.summary:
Applies new settings to an interface at once. Unless they are confirmed
within two minutes (`POST /network/confirm`, from the new address if
it changed), the old settings return by themselves. Needs
`system.manage`.

409.description: `change_pending`, or `refused`: not managed by systemd-networkd, no such interface

get.summary:
Whether the network can be changed here, and a change waiting to be
confirmed. Needs `system.view`.

The channels notifications go out on, besides the interface. Needs
`system.manage`.

post.summary:
Adds a channel: email to recipients, or a webhook. It starts with the
warnings and errors; the routes change that. Needs `system.manage`.

put.summary:
Changes a channel's name, recipients or address, and language. Needs
`system.manage`.

delete.summary:
Removes a channel, and where notifications went on it. Needs
`system.manage`.

post.summary:
Sends a test message on this channel alone now and waits for the
outcome. Needs `system.manage`.

get.summary:
The mail server email channels send through; `null` until one is set
up. Needs `system.manage`.

put.summary:
Sets up the mail server. Without `password` the stored one stays, for
the same server, port, encryption and user name only. Needs
`system.manage`.

get.summary:
Where each kind of notification goes: kept in zendiloOS, and on which
channels. Needs `system.manage`.

put.summary:
Changes where the kinds given go; the others keep theirs. Needs
`system.manage`.

get.summary:
The most recent notifications, newest first, as the signed-in account
left them: what it cleared away is gone, what it read is marked. New ones
arrive on the WebSocket topic `notifications`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most 200; 50 if absent.

post.summary:
Clears the caller's notifications up to `up_to` away; other accounts
still see them.
Marks the caller's notifications up to `up_to` as read, in every browser.

get.summary:
The rules for new passwords; every account may read them. Never
common passwords or ones containing the account name, whatever is set.

put.summary:
Sets the rules for new passwords; passwords already set stay. Needs
`users.manage`.

get.summary: The signed-in account's interface preferences, the same in every browser.

patch.summary:
Changes the signed-in account's interface preferences: only those sent,
a field left out (or `null`) stays as it is. The star prompt only moves
forward.

422.description: `invalid_input`: no such wallpaper name, colour or layout, or a star prompt shown neither once nor twice

get.summary: The blocks in force, the newest first. Needs `system.manage`.

post.summary:
Blocks an address or network until the block is lifted. Needs
`system.manage`.

409.description: `own_address`: the caller would be blocked; `address_allowed`: it is never blocked

get.summary:
The rules, a change waiting for confirmation, the services they can
name with their ports, and those the rules block. Needs
`system.manage`.

put.summary:
Applies new settings at once. Unless confirmed within `confirm_within`
seconds (`POST /security/firewall/confirm`), the rules from before
return by themselves. Settings that would keep out the browser sending
them are refused unless `lock_out` is set. Needs `system.manage`.

502.description: `firewall_failed`: nftables refused the rules; nothing changed

post.summary: Keeps the change waiting for confirmation. Needs `system.manage`.

get.summary:
The sessions of every account that have not ended, the most recently
active first. Needs `system.manage`.

delete.summary:
Ends a session; its browser is signed out with its next request. Needs
`system.manage`.

get.summary:
When sessions end, when accounts lock and addresses are blocked. Needs
`system.manage`.

put.summary:
Sets them; counts of failed attempts start anew where a limit changed,
blocks in place stay. Needs `system.manage`.

post.summary: Lifts a block. Needs `system.manage`.

get.summary: Whether the initial setup is still pending.

post.summary: Creates the first administrator and signs them in.

200.description: Signed in; the session cookie is set.

403.description: `setup_not_local`: an open setup from outside the NAS's own network

get.summary: All shares, ordered by name. Needs `shares.manage`.

post.summary:
Creates a folder directly on a volume: a dataset with its permissions,
offered over SMB (and NFS, if clients are given) while shared. Needs
`shares.manage`.

get.summary:
Every share with an account's or group's rule and what it may do.
Needs `shares.manage`.

put.summary:
Sets an account's or group's rules on several shares at once. Each
share that changes gets its permissions at once and its existing files
in a job. Needs `shares.manage`.

patch.summary:
Changes a share. New permissions apply to the share at once and to its
existing files in a job. Needs `shares.manage`.

409.description: `refused`: rules being applied to the files, or off the network while Macs back up to it

with the job. Needs `shares.manage`.

`shares.manage`.

`shares.manage`.

schedule per frequency. Snapshots of a schedule that is removed stay
until deleted by hand. Needs `shares.manage`.

Deletes one snapshot; the share's data stays as it is. Needs
`shares.manage`.

so are the snapshots taken after it. The share's folder gets the
permissions recorded now at once, its files in a job. Needs
`shares.manage` and the share's name as confirmation; refused while
permissions are being applied to its files.

All disks of the host. Needs `storage.view`.

post.summary:

written) in bursts of 0.7 seconds with pauses between, which flashes
its activity light; a disk asleep wakes. Asked again, it starts over.
NVMe slots mostly have no light. Needs `storage.manage`.

Has the disk test itself; its SMART report shows the progress and then
the result. Needs `storage.manage`.

409.description: `refused`: no SMART, or the disk sleeps

post.summary: Stops the disk's running self-test. Needs `storage.manage`.

parameters.description: Kernel name of the disk, e.g. `sda`

in which slot, the disks in none; while nothing is chosen, the model

get.summary: The NAS models zendiloOS knows. Needs `storage.view`.

delete.summary: Forgets a disk that is no longer present. Needs `storage.manage`.

get.summary: The disks blinking now. Needs `storage.view`.

Every concern about pools and disks in one place, the worst first.
SMART verdicts are the monitor's last ones (read every six hours), so
this reads no disk. Needs `storage.view`.

The ZFS pools. Fails if ZFS is unavailable, e.g. when its kernel module
could not be built for a new kernel. Needs `storage.view`.

post.summary:
Creates the pool of a plan, erasing its disks. The disks are checked
again first: if anything changed since the plan, nothing happens.
Answers with the job. Needs `storage.manage`.

Plans a new pool: which disks would be erased and what the pool would
offer. Erases nothing. Needs `storage.manage`.

Destroys a pool zendiloOS created and erases its disks. All its data is
lost. Refused while shares, apps, the personal folders or Docker's data
live on it (`pool_in_use`, the detail names them). Answers with the job.
Needs `storage.manage`.

409.description: `pool_not_managed`; `pool_in_use`: the detail names what lives on it

post.summary:
Carries out a planned replacement; ZFS then resilvers onto the new disk.
Answers with the job. Needs `storage.manage`.

Plans replacing a device of a pool with another disk. Erases nothing.
Needs `storage.manage`.

Starts checking all data of the pool; progress shows in the pool.
Needs `storage.manage`.

Stops the pool's scrub; what it checked so far stays checked. A resilver
cannot be stopped. Needs `storage.manage`.

get.summary:
The removable drives plugged in. New ones are mounted while they are
listed, as on Windows; zendiloOS also looks once a minute by itself.
Needs `storage.manage`.

post.summary:
Ejects a drive: unmounts it, refused while files on it are open, and
powers its disk off. Needs `storage.manage`.

404.description: `not_found`: no such drive is plugged in

post.summary:
Mounts a drive that was ejected, or that could not be mounted before;
as it is if it is mounted. Needs `storage.manage`.

404.description: `not_found`: no such drive is plugged in

409.description: `refused`: the agent's checks, in its words

get.summary: When the disks test themselves. Needs `storage.view`.

put.summary:

get.summary: The data volumes. Needs `storage.view`.
Facts about the host and the installed Zendiloos version.

What the dashboard's charts show before live samples arrive over the
WebSocket (topic `metrics`).

post.summary:
Reboots or powers off the system. Needs `system.manage`. Refused while

get.summary:
What there is to update, what is going on and how the NAS looks for

Installs what the last check found: Debian's packages, then zendiloOS,
whose interface restarts on the way. A restart of the NAS is asked for
separately. Needs `system.manage`. Refused while background jobs run
(`jobs_running`, the detail names them): the agents would see them

Looks for a newer release and for Debian's updates, in the background;
the overview says when it is done. Needs `system.manage`.

put.summary:
Which releases are offered and whether the NAS looks daily. Needs
`system.manage`.

The web interface's ports and certificate, and a change waiting to be

reloaded. Unless they are confirmed within `confirm_within` seconds
(`POST /system/web-server/confirm`, from the new address), the old ones
return by themselves. Needs `system.manage`.
